blocks.intendedMeaning: Chemical evidence historically established atoms and molecules. The original expects earlier grade-six physics and grade-seven chemistry; this unit instead examines a device that produces an image related to individual atomic positions and estimates size.
conditions: Chemical evidence is mentioned, not enumerated or newly proved in this block.
uncertainties: Historical firstness is a source account, not a newly verified priority claim. For an eight-year-old, prior-school-course dependence must not prevent independent reading.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Describe the source's ion projector/field-ion microscope: spherical container, sharp central tungsten tip, conducting luminescent inner surface, positive tip, negative coating and low-pressure helium.
numbers: tip curvature radius about 5 x 10^-6 cm
conditions: These are the described source-device parameters, not certified universal/current apparatus values or build instructions.
uncertainties: Real field-ion apparatus operation is not established by reading this passage; do not certify the quoted voltage/pressure as sufficient.
figureLimits: Figure 2 reference only; no geometry, coating layout or electrode topology can be approved without its independent image review.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Place the Figure 2 apparatus illustration at this source location.
figureLimits: Empty source text is not evidence of the unreviewed drawing's objects or correctness.
Caption identity only, not image approval.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Place the Figure 3 tip/projection illustration at this source location.
figureLimits: No inspection or endorsement of diagram labels, angular construction or particle depiction.
Caption identity only, not image approval.

blocks.intendedMeaning: The source depicts tungsten surface atoms as small protrusions and describes helium losing electrons in a strong electric field near the tip. Positive helium ions move outward and strike a luminescent screen, yielding an enlarged map related to the surface atomic arrangement.
conditions: Distinguish neutral helium from positive ions, field-driven ionization from ordinary mechanical impact, and ion-screen imaging from ordinary optical photography.
uncertainties: The source's literal collision account and ideal radial paths are simplified; acceptable attribution must not make them universal necessary microscopic mechanisms.
figureLimits: No unreviewed Figure 3 relief or recorded tungsten image may be interpreted or certified.

blocks.intendedMeaning: In the source's ideal concentric spherical radial-projection model, corresponding tip and screen arcs subtend the same angle; their ratio equals the ratio of the radii and gives a magnification estimate.
numbers: 10 / (5 x 10^-6) = 2 x 10^6 using matching centimeter units
conditions: R is container/screen radius; r is tip-curvature radius; alpha is a common central angle measured in radians; ab and AB are arc lengths, not arbitrary chords.
uncertainties: This is a geometrical estimate, not guaranteed magnification for arbitrary real field-ion instruments.
figureLimits: The drawing's placement of a, b, A, B and alpha is not reviewed; the textual proof can be reviewed independently.

conditions: An ion-screen image is an indirect imaging record, not a literal optical photograph resolving atom outlines.
figureLimits: No counting of spots, crystallographic interpretation, photographic provenance or image fidelity approval.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Estimate tungsten atomic size using neighboring center spacing in an adjoining-particle model. Divide measured screen spacing by magnification to infer tip spacing. Other atomic/molecular dimensions are of similar order of magnitude.
conditions: Size-as-center-spacing is a model-dependent estimate, not an atom's hard visible boundary or one diameter shared by all species.
uncertainties: No AB measurement is supplied in the text; the quoted value remains the source estimate, not a measurement this review has reproduced.
figureLimits: No actual spacing measurement from the unreviewed image.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Give a source hydrogen-molecule size estimate and use the same magnification for a pen and a molecule to convey scale: an Earth-to-Moon-sized enlarged pen would make the molecule comparable to the original pen.
numbers: hydrogen molecule size estimate 2.3 x 10^-8 cm
conditions: One common scale factor; original pen length and Earth-Moon distance assumptions determine the comparison; this is a rough illustration.
uncertainties: No pen length or Earth-Moon distance is numerically specified; exact equality or arbitrary-pen universality would be unsupported. Molecular diameter is model-dependent.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Atoms and molecules are too small for naked-eye or ordinary optical-microscope resolution, so matter appears continuous at those scales.
conditions: Appearance of continuity is not actual absence of microscopic structure; do not claim every type of microscope is incapable of atomic imaging.

blocks.intendedMeaning: Estimate the number of water molecules in about 1 gram or 1 cubic centimeter of water by assigning each molecule a closely packed occupied-volume cell.
conditions: Water density near 1 g/cm^3; approximate occupied volume/close-packing model, not exact molecular cube shape or immutable density. (3 x 10^-8)^3 = 2.7 x 10^-23 rounds to 3 x 10^-23.
uncertainties: Approximate count and model assumptions must remain visible; no invented correction or falsely exact count.

blocks.intendedMeaning: A breath contains enormously many molecules; if an exhaled breath's molecules were uniformly mixed throughout Earth's atmosphere, a later breath could contain a small expected share, illustrated by the source as two molecules.
numbers: comparison with preceding enormous molecule count
conditions: Hypothetical complete uniform global mixing; assumed breath size and atmospheric amount; random sampling/average rather than a guaranteed integer per person per breath.
uncertainties: No mixing time, breath volume or atmospheric molecule total is specified; do not guarantee instant global distribution, exactly two for everyone, or equal water/breath counts.
